newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar recovery dents regionals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar recovery dents regionals.

text.p: The U.S. dollar's partial overnight recovery and continued firm tone against the major currencies weighed on most regional currencies on Wednesday.
In Malaysia, the ringgit weakened on the dollar's rise and commercial demand for the dollar from Kuala Lumpur, dealers said.
"There's been some buying interest in dollar/ringgit. It was taken to a high of 2.5247 in the morning," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
She said dollar/ringgit showed potential for further gains but would need to break through the 2.5300 resistance.
Dealers said the market showed little reaction to Malaysia's positive trade figures announced on Saturday because of a holiday on Monday.
Some dealers said they expected a stronger ringgit after it broke through a key resistance level against the Singapore dollar at 0.5550.
"At the current levels, I see a stronger ringgit. Many may re-establish their ringgit/Sing positions. It (long ringgit) is a positive carry," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
Across the border, the Singapore dollar slipped slightly in quiet trade as players covered their short U.S. dollar positions after the U.S. dollar's recent drop below S$1.4000.
"The market was caught short after being sold down to a low of 1.3967 in the last two days," said the European bank dealer.
She said players had scrambled to cover their short positions after detecting U.S. dollar buying by local banks on Tuesday, possibly on behalf of the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

"The market was oversold below the 1.40 level and there was a panic when the big local boys came in around 1.3970/80," she said, adding however, that the U.S. unit was likely to keep to a range of S$1.3990-1.4035 for the time being.
"I don't think it's going to move either way," she said.

The Indonesian rupiah held steady in slow dealings, as the possibility of a higher central bank fixing kept players from selling the dollar below the 2,335.0 level despite firm sentiment on the rupiah.

A European bank dealer in Jakarta said the central bank had depreciated the rupiah by 13 points in the past four weeks, with four points posted last week, leading operators to speculate on a similar depreciation target by the central bank for this week. Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,334/2,526 and the conversion rate to 2,334/2,382 on Tuesday.
A Japanese bank dealer said ample liquidity was another factor to consider but its impact was being limited by sustained bullish sentiment on the rupiah.
"We do look at the liquidity. But the rupiah keeps hovering at the higher end of the central bank band. This might be the equilibrium level," he said.
The European bank dealer said swap rates remained soft due to the liquidity factor but people seemed to feel it might have bottomed out for now.
"There are some coverings this morning because many players appear to be feeling uncomfortable. The rebound could be very fast on any minor issue," the dealer said.
The Thai baht slid on the back of the dollar's rise against the majors and persistent demand for the U.S. unit.
"Dollar buying continued at a high level compared to the central bank's fixing," said a currency dealer in Bangkok. "The U.S. unit is also on the uptrend in overseas markets."
The overnight interbank rate remained high on strong demand for funds as banks began borrowing early for the reserve requirement and the payment of value added tax.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
